title: Use typed initialization
why: Zeroing a complete object's representation bypasses typed initialization and may not produce a valid value for its C++ type.
suggestion: Consider typed initialization or assignment when the object's semantics permit it; do not replace intentional byte-level buffer clearing with value initialization.
limitations: Requires memset, std::memset, or ::memset with an address-of simple object identifier, literal 0, and sizeof of the identical identifier; multiline calls are supported.
Does not report runtime pointer ranges, indexed or member expressions, pointer offsets, arbitrary byte counts, or nonmatching sizeof targets.
Lexically masks comments and ordinary, continued, and raw string literals; does not resolve macros, overloads, object types, initialization lifetimes, or representation equivalence.
